subexperiment: native fixed-window reader with natural merges and 84 simultaneous inserts ABBA

protocol.source: Full native prometheusQueryRange(avg by(scope)(avg_over_time(tslab_r02_periodic[30m]))) fixed at end of first 12 batches; newer inserts have greater timestamps, so independent Python oracle must stay constant.
protocol.query_cache: use_query_cache=0, independent from R11 cache hit
protocol.natural_merges: ON, no STOP MERGES or forced OPTIMIZE
protocol.read_stats: Only completed query requests whose start and end both fall inside the writer's active window; query-log CPU and physical part stats preserved
protocol.validation: all four phases correctness success; 74/82/81/75 full overlapped native queries across phases; exact labels, time and values within 1e-8; no OOM; A/A drift under 25%

math_bound: Same underlying 96-batch payload and read oracle in all modes. This is a mixed workload, so raw/LC process CPU includes ingest + native query + naturally scheduled merges. A fixed query evaluation time over only the first 12 batches prevents output changes from causing latency differences. Read p95 can still be affected by uneven sampling over table growth; progress quartile per read is recorded. A/A p95 drift 14.16%, raw p95 is 18.12% lower on one runner, so do not promote before independent runner replication and quartile-matched audit.
limitations: One runner, two same-runner phase medians per type; near-threshold p95 relative effect requires replication.
Read p95 distributions contain 74-82 fully overlapped requests per phase, not identical query counts. Progress stratification may be necessary to attribute effects.
Fixed 12-batch query selects only a small historical window; no high cardinality exact branch filter or 14-day lookback.
No deliberate memory limit stress or 400-node production churn; stock O1 glibc build and synthetic data.
CPU mix combines query, write, and natural merge work. This test does not decompose components the way 96-batch stopped-merge test did.
